title: Start a service business
pitch: Get your first paying client from nothing.
opening: A few quick questions so your team knows you.
Pick a number or say it your own way. There are no wrong answers.

questions.line: What can you do that someone would pay for?

choices.label: Build or fix websites and tools
choices.says: building and fixing websites and tools

choices.label: Sort out messy work: books, schedules, inboxes
choices.says: sorting out messy back office work

questions.line: Who do you want to do it for?
What headache would you take off their plate?

choices.label: The job that eats their evenings
choices.says: the job that eats their evenings

choices.label: The thing they keep putting off
choices.says: the thing they keep putting off

choices.label: The work only they can do, so it piles up
choices.says: the work that piles up because only they can do it

choices.label: The gap that is costing them customers
choices.says: the gap that is costing them customers

questions.line: How many hours a week can you really give this? Pick the honest one.
A year from now, what would make you proud?

choices.label: Someone I never met pays me
choices.says: someone you never met pays you

choices.label: A client comes back a second time
choices.says: a client comes back a second time

choices.label: I can say no to work I do not want
choices.says: you can say no to work you do not want

questions.line: What number would tell you this is working? Say it your way.

Not sure yet? Press enter. You can add it later.

mission: A one-person service for {clients} that takes away {pain}.

will: Sell one thing to one kind of client.
Name one price. A real number, never a range.
Do the homework on a person before you write to them.
Follow up twice. Most yeses come after the second note.
Get paid before you build anything made just for them.
will_not: Send the same note to a hundred people.
Count a kind reply as a win. Only money counts.
Chase someone who needs the whole idea explained before they see the value.
Send anything you did not write and approve.

your_part: You pick the offer and the price.
You write and send every note. Nothing goes out without you.
You answer the questions or take the call.
You say when the work is good enough to hand over.

team.name: researcher
team.job: Finds real owners who fit and does the homework on each one.

team.name: editor
team.job: Tightens your offer and your notes without changing your voice.

team.name: keeper
team.job: Keeps every person, reply and follow-up date in one list.

team.name: maker
team.job: Helps you do the work and checks it before the client sees it.

chapters.title: One offer
chapters.finish_line: You approved one sentence: who it is for, what you fix and one price.
chapters.take: Pick the smallest job you could finish in a week. Small offers get a yes. Big ones get a meeting.

moves.you: Write the headache the way your client would say it at 9pm. One sentence, their words.
moves.brief: Do not write this for them. When the sentence arrives, save it as it is in {run_dir}/their-words.md.

moves.you: Your editor turns that sentence into three ways to say your offer, with the price left blank.
moves.brief: Read {run_dir}/their-words.md. Write three one-sentence offers for {clients}: who it is for and the one thing fixed, using {skill}. Each must be a job one person can finish in a week. Leave the price blank. Never use the words AI, agent or automate. Save as {run_dir}/offer-drafts.md.

moves.you: Pick one price. Choose a number they could say yes to without asking anyone.
moves.brief: The price is theirs. If they ask for help, say what the offer saves the client in hours or money and let them choose. Never pick the number.

moves.you: Pick the offer that sounds like you and add your price. Say it out loud once.
moves.brief: This call is theirs. Save the chosen sentence with the price as {run_dir}/offer.md.

chapters.title: Twenty real people
chapters.finish_line: 20 owners on your list, each checked by hand, each with one true detail.
chapters.take: Twenty people you studied beat two hundred you copied from a list. Owners who answer their own email are the ones who reply.

moves.you: Your researcher writes the rule for who fits, so nobody wastes a note.
moves.brief: Write the fit rule for {clients} in four lines: they decide alone, they feel {pain} every week, they answer their own email, they are small enough that the price is a real choice. Add who to skip: big companies and anyone who wants free custom work first. Save as {run_dir}/who-fits.md.

moves.you: Your researcher finds twenty real owners who fit, each with one true detail.
moves.brief: Find 20 owners among {clients} who match {run_dir}/who-fits.md. For each: name, business, town, the page they control where their contact is printed, and one true recent detail with its link. Read public pages only, never one behind a sign-in. Mark an address you could not see on their own page as unconfirmed. Never guess an address. Save as {run_dir}/people.md.

moves.you: Read the list. Cross off anyone you would not enjoy working for. Star the ten you want most.
moves.brief: The picks are theirs. Keep the crossed off names out of every later step.
moves.proof_hint: how many stayed and how many you starred

chapters.title: Ten notes sent
chapters.finish_line: 10 notes sent, each written by you, each about one person.
chapters.take: The first note is not a pitch. It shows you noticed something real, names one price and asks one question they can answer in a line.

moves.you: Your researcher does the homework on your ten: three facts each and the one problem they point at.
moves.brief: For each starred person in {run_dir}/people.md, spend ten minutes. Note three public facts (town, years open, one recent post) and the one problem they already talk about, in their own words, with links. Say so when a detail is thin. Save as {run_dir}/homework.md.

moves.you: Write one note to the person you most want. Four lines: their problem in their words, what you would do, your price, one small question.
moves.brief: They write every word. If they ask, the editor may cut words, never add ideas. No call or meeting ask in the first note. Save their note as {run_dir}/first-note.md.

moves.you: Send ten notes, one person at a time, each changed to fit that person. Your proof is the count and the day.
moves.brief: Only they send. Never send or schedule a message for them and never send to many at once. After each send, the keeper adds the person and the day to {run_dir}/sent.md.
moves.proof_hint: how many you sent and when

chapters.title: First real conversation
chapters.finish_line: One owner replied and you answered their questions or talked for twenty minutes.
chapters.take: Follow up on day 5 and day 12, then stop. Every follow-up brings one new idea. Never write just checking in.

moves.you: Your keeper puts a follow-up date next to every note you sent.
moves.brief: For each person in {run_dir}/sent.md, write two follow-up dates: 5 days and 12 days after the send. After the second with no reply, mark them quiet and stop. Save as {run_dir}/follow-ups.md.

moves.you: Your researcher finds one useful idea for each person who has not replied.
moves.brief: For each person due a follow-up, find one specific idea that helps them with {pain}, from something public and new since the first note. One line each with its link. Save as {run_dir}/follow-up-ideas.md. Ideas only, never a written message.

moves.you: Write and send the follow-ups that are due. One new idea each, two lines.
moves.brief: Only they write and send. Never offer a third follow-up to the same person.

moves.you: When someone replies, say their problem back in their words. If they agree that is the problem, tell them your price.
moves.brief: The conversation is theirs. Keep calls to twenty minutes. If the person has to be convinced there is a problem, they are not the first client. Note what they said they need in {run_dir}/replies.md.
moves.proof_hint: who replied and what they said they need

chapters.title: First paid job
chapters.finish_line: One client paid you, the work is handed over and you wrote down why they said yes.
chapters.take: Get paid before you start. Someone who wants free custom work first is not your first client.

moves.you: Ask for the yes in one message: the job, the price and the day you start.
moves.brief: They write and send it. One job, one price, one start day. No extras and no discount unless they choose one.

moves.you: Get paid before you start. Make paying easy, in the money they use.
moves.brief: Only they take the payment. A kind reply or a promise is not a payment. Count it only when the money arrives.

moves.you: Your maker writes the short list that says when this job is done.
moves.brief: Read {run_dir}/offer.md and {run_dir}/replies.md. Write five lines or fewer that say what done means for this client, each one checkable. Save as {run_dir}/done-list.md. Help with the work when asked and check it against the list before it goes out.

moves.you: Hand over the work. Then ask one question: what made you say yes? Write the answer down. It is your pitch now.
moves.brief: They hand it over and ask the question. Save the client's answer, in the client's words, as {run_dir}/why-yes.md.
moves.proof_hint: the payment and why they said yes
